metadata.description: Restaurants and Hotels CPI indices (COICOP CP11) for all 8 currencies. Covers meals and non-alcoholic drinks consumed outside the home: restaurants, cafes, fast food, canteens, and accommodation services.
metadata.indexBase: 2015=100 for GBP, EUR, CAD, CHF, NZD, JPY. USD: 1982-84=100 native (BLS CUUR0000SEFV). AUD: 2011-Q3=100 native.

sources.USD: BLS CPI-U Food Away from Home (CUUR0000SEFV), native base 1982-84=100.
sources.GBP: ONS CPI Restaurants and Hotels (COICOP CP11), 2015=100. FRED GBRCP110000IXNBQ (2000-2022), ONS CPI detailed reference tables 2023-2025.
sources.EUR: Eurostat HICP Euro area (EA) CP11 Restaurants and Hotels, annual average 2015=100. Dataset: prc_hicp_aind.
sources.CAD: Statistics Canada CPI Food Purchased from Restaurants. FRED CANCP110000IXNBM (2015-2022), Stats Canada Table 18-10-0004-01 YoY rates 2023-2025.
sources.AUD: ABS CPI Hotels, Cafes and Restaurants (COICOP CP11). FRED AUSCP110000IXNBQ (2012-2022), ABS CPI quarterly release annual YoY rates 2023-2025.
sources.CHF: Swiss FSO CPI Restaurants and Hotels (CP11). FRED CP1100CHM086NEST (2005-2025, complete).
sources.JPY: Statistics Bureau of Japan CPI Eating Out. FRED JPNCP110000GPM monthly, annual averages computed. 2021-2025 from Japan Stats Bureau annual CPI release (2020=100), chain-linked.
sources.NZD: Stats NZ CPI Restaurant Meals and Ready-to-Eat Food (COICOP CP11). FRED NZLCP110000IXNBQ (2007-2022), Stats NZ Infoshare annual rates 2023-2025.

metadata.notes: USD Food Away from Home has risen consistently faster than overall CPI, driven by labour costs. Japan's eating-out category remained nearly flat 2000-2020 (deflationary era) then surged post-2022 on energy and food input cost pass-through. CHF restaurants are the most expensive globally in absolute terms but have relatively low inflation due to already-high base prices.
